newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australian Broadcasting Corp Midday Update.
newsitem.headline: Australian Broadcasting Corp Midday Update.

text.p: BEAZLEY SAYS HOWARD FORGETFULNESS BEYOND BELIEF
The Federal Opposition Leader, Kim Beazley, says the Prime Minister has displayed a curious forgetfulness about being told late last year Federal Police were investigating Liberal Senator Bob Woods.
Mr Howard said earlier this week that Senator Woods first told him eleven days ago that his use of parliamentary expenses was being investigated.
However Mr Howard has now revealed he was briefed about the matter late last year by Attorney-General, Daryl Williams.
Mr Beazley says it beggars belief that the Prime Minister could have forgotten a briefing about a member of his executive and a person so close to him.
FISCHER DEFENDS HOWARD ON WOODS AFFAIR
The Deputy Prime Minister says John Howard moved quickly last night to set the record straight on when he first knew of allegations against Liberal Senator Bob Woods.
The Prime Minister says he first knew about allegations concerning Liberal Senator Bob Woods' use of parliamentary expenses late last year.
Earlier this week, Mr Howard said Senator Woods, first told him of them less than a fortnight ago.
Tim Fischer asks if former Prime Minister Paul Keating would have moved quickly to clarify the situation, as Mr Howard did last night.
Senator Woods, who's denying the allegations, will be leaving Parliament next month.
EXTREME WEATHER IN THREE STATES
Extreme weather conditions are having an effect on three states with Victoria's heatwave continuing, flash flooding in South Australia's north, and flooding in western Queensland.
Weather forecasters in Melbourne say it's unusual that the heatwave has continued for nearly a week.
Temperatures around the state are expected to stay in the mid-thirties until a mild change on Sunday.
The Weather Bureau warns there could be further flash flooding in parts of South Australia's far north.
A family at Bon Bon station, south of Coober Pedy, were forced out of the homestead as 175-millimetres of rain fell in four hours.
In western Queensland, the clean up continues after floods in Charleville, but several roads remain cut.
There's at least one-and-a-half metres of water across the Mitchell Highway south of Charleville.
AUSSIE HOME LOANS TIPS INTEREST CUT
Australia's biggest non-bank home lender, Aussie Home Loans, says it's now a matter of "when, not if" official interest rates fall again.
And it's lowered its two and three-year fixed loan rates in the expectation easier monetary policy will be delivered sometime in the next two months.
The board of the Reserve Bank met on Tuesday, but there was no signal on rates yesterday morning when an announcement might normally have been expected.

Aussie Home Loans managing director, John Symond, says Australia is entrenched in a low inflation and low interest rate cycle, and borrowers can expect to enjoy low, stable rates over the next few years.
SCHOOLS MINISTER EMBRACES EMPLOYMENT SCHEME
Schools Minister David Kemp says many schools now want to make sure their school leavers get jobs.
Doctor Kemp says schools are among contractors hired under the Government's job brokers scheme to find work for students not opting to go to university.
The scheme will be trialled for three-months with community groups and job agencies also hired to find work for school leavers.
Doctor Kemp says a lot of schools are now taking the view that teaching the basic skills and helping students understand the world outside the school, is not quite enough.
DAVIS CUP TEAM NAMED
In tennis, Mark Woodforde and Patrick Rafter are to represent Australia in the singles of the Davis Cup tie against France starting tomorrow at Sydney's White City.
The two were named by captain John Newcombe after long deliberations, which saw a number of matches played yesterday before final decisions were made.
The make-up of the team to take on the Cup holders was made more difficult with logical choices Mark Philippoussis and Jason Stoltenberg absent because of injury.
Todd Woodbridge and Woodforde will play the doubles.
DARWIN HAS NATION'S MOST EXPENSIVE POWER
A new national survey shows electricity prices in Darwin are Australia's most expensive.
The survey by National Utility Services also shows Canberra customers paid the biggest increase in prices over the last 12-months, of three-point-seven-percent.

The biggest drop has been experienced by Sydney electricity consumers...the survey shows their prices fell by three-percent. In summing up the survey, National Utility Services says it's seen enough industry deregulation to say that market forces won't automatically send prices lower.
-- Reuters Sydney Newsroom 61-2 9373-1800
